newsitem.title: UK: Nationwide calls for UK society bill.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide calls for UK society bill.

text.p: One of Britain's largest building societies, the Nationwide, on Tuesday called on the British government to introduce the new Building Societies Bill in the current session of parliament.

The new bill, which would remove a current five-year protection from hostile takeovers for newly converted societies, has been criticised by some institutions in the process of converting from mutual societies to public limited companies.

"The complaints by some converting societies on this issue imply that they feel they need to rely on unfair, anti- competitive protection to survive as independent organisations," Nationwide chief executive Brian Davis said.

Davies, who was speaking at a building societies conference in London on Tuesday, said the bill would give societies the flexibility to continue to provide strong competition, "which benefits the nation's consumers through better rates and service."

"We hope that parliament will be firm in addressing this issue and not be swayed by veiled threats of delaying conversion windfall payments," Davis said. The Nationwide has ruled out converting to a public limited company.
